function: Geolocation-to-precoder mapping for feedback-free downlink MIMO: VAE picks representative SVD precoders, GPR predicts them at unseen locations; RI and CQI by statistics and interpolation (pp. 4, 7-9)
system: DL SU-MIMO OFDM: BS 16 dual-polarized Tx antennas (8,1), UE 4 Rx, 72 subcarriers, 3.5 GHz, 15 kHz spacing; no RIS (p. 9)
method: VAE (fully connected, 3 hidden layers, unsupervised) compresses SVD precoders; Gaussian process regression (supervised) infers latent variables at new locations; trained offline on historical channels (pp. 9-10)
data_channel: DeepMIMO O1 ray tracing converted to CDL channels per 3GPP TR 38.901; BS1, user grid 1, 3780 training and 945 testing locations, 100 time samples (pp. 9-10, 14)
test_conditions: Train: 3780 locations (126 rows), 100 time samples; test: 945 other locations (63 rows) in the same O1 scenario and BS, 80/20 split; no new scenario (p. 10)
baselines: Non-learned: 5G CLSM (Type I codebook feedback, with and without 1-TTI delay), SVD precoder, own statistic-based codebook solutions 1-3; learned: only variants of own VAE (pp. 10-13)
metrics: Average throughput (Mbps) from link-level simulation; throughput loss or gain relative to 5G CLSM (%); reconstruction throughput of VAE precoders; locations with zero throughput (pp. 10-13)
q1_support: p. 9: "realistic ray-tracing dataset: DeepMIMO [42]". The CDL channels are built "according to standard [43]", which is 3GPP TR 38.901 v16.1.0 (reference list, p. 14).
q2_support: p. 10: "the testing set is made up of channels generated between BS1 and UEs of 63 rows". Test locations are held out from the same DeepMIMO O1 scenario and BS (80/20 split); no other scenario, band, antenna number or adaptation is tested.
q3_support: p. 12: "Fig. 13 shows the average throughput comparison of CLSM and proposed solutions for data-driven MIMO at all locations in H." Non-learned baselines exist (CLSM, SVD), but no earlier learned method is compared; the only learned models are the paper's own VAE variants.
q4_support: p. 10: "they are both designed as fully connected neural networks with 3 hidden layers". Only the architecture and layer sizes are given; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported anywhere in the paper.
q5_support: p. 9: "realistic ray-tracing dataset: DeepMIMO [42]". Public DeepMIMO channels (scenario O1) are used for training and testing; no link to the authors' own code or data is given.
notes: PDF is arXiv v1 (24 Nov 2023, p. 1) of the TMC paper; the DOI is not printed in the file, but title and authors match. Area 3: the learned part outputs the BS precoder; RI and CQI come from mode statistics and nearest-neighbor or Voronoi interpolation (link-adaptation-like, pp. 5-6, 9). The codebook-based approach (pp. 5-6) is statistical, not neural. Area 2 was considered (feedback elimination), but no channel is estimated or predicted. q2: the Nrx=1 versus Nrx=4 comparison (Fig. 5, p. 10) re-derives the fixed parameters for each setting, so it is not a test in new conditions.
